01.purpose: A voluntary bill-check service could help households find concessions, billing mistakes, unnecessary fees and alternative offers. Savings would be measured after switching costs.
01.redlandsAdaptation: Residents could access bill checks through existing library and community channels, supported by secure document handling and a dated referral guide. Participation and any initial case checks would require the household’s consent.
01.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for accessible bill-check assistance through libraries and community partners. Document handling and referrals would be based on residents’ consent.
01.conflictBoundary: If council considered selecting Luke’s bill-check software, Strange But True or a related adviser, that transaction would require independent handling. Referral criteria would disclose any commercial relationship.

02.purpose: The legal information engine could reduce the time residents spend finding the applicable rule, gathering documents and reaching the right service.
02.redlandsAdaptation: A Redlands version could explain council processes, common consumer issues and routes to help. Source dates, the applicable jurisdiction and a plain-language complaint trail would accompany the information.
02.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for a rules and referral navigator covering council processes, with dated sources and connections to community legal assistance.
02.conflictBoundary: Any council licence or contract involving Luke’s legal-engine intellectual property would require independent assessment. Case referrals and document access would use clear consent and impartial criteria.

03.purpose: Owners and occupants could use a body corporate navigator to understand charges, compare procurement options and find existing dispute pathways.
03.redlandsAdaptation: A checklist tailored to each scheme could cover levies, budgets, insurance, maintenance, meeting rights, records requests and disputed by-laws. It would identify the applicable statutory regime and routes to professional help.
03.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring owners, occupants and advice providers together and seek information and referral support through council’s community functions.
03.conflictBoundary: A general information service would be separate from any council transaction involving Luke’s software or business. Each participating scheme would choose its own advisers and procurement arrangements.

04.purpose: Council could prepare for advancing AI in its own work through accountable human decisions, useful staff support and reliable public services.
04.redlandsAdaptation: The proposal includes a council AI operating policy and practical service and workflow demonstrations. These would cover records, data access, workforce support, procurement, cyber resilience, continuity and human review. Shared capacity could support different operational needs without requiring every service to use one programme.
04.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could build support for council’s AI policy and service objectives, with implementation, staff involvement and reporting managed through the CEO.
04.conflictBoundary: Any council purchase, licence or service arrangement connected to Luke’s AI software, training, support or financial interests would be assessed as a specific transaction under the applicable interest rules.

05.purpose: Residents, community groups and small businesses could build practical AI and data sovereignty skills through free entry options and low-cost further learning.
05.redlandsAdaptation: Accessible online lessons and optional supported sessions could cover useful prompts, source checking, scams, document privacy, backups, exporting data, local models and choosing providers. Suitable free official training could be included.
05.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for accessible online resources, library and community learning, and partnerships with education and digital-inclusion providers.
05.conflictBoundary: If council funded teaching, licensed Luke’s learning materials or purchased support from Strange But True, the related interest would be identified and handled through the applicable decision process.

06.purpose: Residents could spend less time making repeat calls, correcting incomplete applications or travelling to resolve routine council matters.
06.redlandsAdaptation: Councillors, residents and staff could identify forms and processes that cause repeated difficulty. Plain-language guidance, assisted forms, accessible status tracking and a verified council knowledge layer could then be trialled.
06.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek service improvements and a council decision on the experience residents should receive. The CEO would manage integration with existing systems.
06.conflictBoundary: Any council purchase, licence or integration involving Luke’s software or Strange But True would require independent assessment and procurement. Resident case information would remain within the authorised service workflow.

07.purpose: Residents and businesses could explore source-linked public civic data, compare ideas for particular places and submit proposals that others can reproduce and examine.
07.redlandsAdaptation: A council dataset and rights catalogue could identify approved public layers, scenario assumptions and proposal-export formats. Reproducible simulations of selected civic questions could use public, synthetic or appropriately de-identified information, with the relevant data owners involved.
07.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek a council data-access policy and useful public simulation services. Staff and data owners would determine approved datasets, update responsibilities and integration.
07.conflictBoundary: Any council decision involving a data licence, simulation tool, software licence or data-service agreement would identify relevant interests, including Luke’s where applicable.

08.purpose: Voluntary C-hours could recognise useful contributions, help people exchange skills and make community work easier to organise.
08.redlandsAdaptation: Willing hosts could develop contribution opportunities across care, repairs, gardens, digital help, arts and preparedness. Following the September 2026 C-hour direction, records would connect actual activities and outcomes with freely given time, verification, reflection and each participant’s choices about information sharing.
08.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring willing hosts together, support community discussion of verification and participation, and seek council consideration of venues or support for a voluntary C-hour demonstration.
08.conflictBoundary: Luke’s C-hour tools, intellectual property or delivery role would be relevant interests if council funded, hosted or commissioned a contribution programme involving them.

09.purpose: Communities could shape recognition and reciprocal opportunities around what participants value and what hosts can offer.
09.redlandsAdaptation: Residents and hosts could consider shared meals, skill exchanges, tool access, learning, events and other affordable forms of thanks. Ideas, delivery costs, donated capacity and access rules would be recorded before choosing trials.
09.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring residents, hosts and businesses together to discuss recognition they would value or offer. Any council contribution would follow its own decision process.
09.conflictBoundary: Luke’s tools, equipment or provider role would be identified if council considered funding a reciprocal offer or selecting him to supply it.

10.purpose: Ready SET Co-op is a proposal for a member-governed organisation that could coordinate work, administration, shared assets and services across participating projects.
10.redlandsAdaptation: Prospective members could develop the rules, governance, financial model, paid-work and training pathways, insurance, administration and service arrangements. Agreements would specify what the co-operative would own, operate or provide, and how it would work with each host or partner.
10.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could convene discussion about co-operative public-benefit delivery. Council could consider relevant support or service arrangements through its own processes.
10.conflictBoundary: Any proposed membership, paid role, asset or contractual interest held by Luke would be identified when council considered an arrangement with the co-operative.

11.purpose: Community organisations could reduce repeated application work and make funding, procurement and delivery obligations easier to follow and demonstrate.
11.redlandsAdaptation: Public resources could help organisations assess eligibility and whether to apply, assemble evidence, prepare budgets, track obligations, control documents, complete acquittals and check conflicts. Applicant assistance would remain separate from the funder’s or purchaser’s assessment.
11.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek accessible capability support for organisations and clear council information about grants and procurement. Live assessments would remain with the responsible decision-makers.
11.conflictBoundary: Any connection between Luke and an applicant, a paid application-support service or a tender would be identified where council was providing assistance or making a decision.

12.purpose: State and federal investment could support the coordination, infrastructure, skills and ongoing operation needed for locally governed capability and services.
12.redlandsAdaptation: Luke’s public submissions could inform a Redlands funding case that identifies public purposes, service responsibilities, participating organisations, capital and operating accounts, local contributions and the decisions sought from each government or institution. Distinct project cases could support shared regional requests where councils chose to participate.
12.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could present a council-endorsed case to responsible state and federal portfolios and funding institutions, bring local MPs and delivery partners together, and coordinate negotiations with willing neighbouring councils.
12.conflictBoundary: Any proposed allocation, funded role or agreement directly benefiting Luke’s project, business or associated organisation would be identified within the funding request.

13.purpose: GAJRA Earth Redlands could be a locally shaped association and network for shared purpose, learning, community work and reciprocal capability.
13.redlandsAdaptation: Prospective participants could shape its purpose, membership, governance, legal structure and connections with participating projects and other GAJRA communities. Its own activities would be distinguished from those of independent people, organisations and delivery partners.
13.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could convene discussion of public purposes and community connections. Any council relationship with a particular association would be considered through the relevant council process.
13.conflictBoundary: Any GAJRA role or financial interest held by Luke would be identified when council considered a grant, premises arrangement, service agreement or other support for the association.

14.title: Luke’s personal HBOT purchase and Genesis journey
14.purpose: Luke’s proposed personal Genesis journey would develop the relationship between a person and their Aura and carry that learning into everyday life.
14.redlandsAdaptation: Luke proposes to buy his own HBOT equipment and establish his first Genesis journey. The setting, personal Aura, chosen records and permissions, reflection and everyday application would follow his purposes. Genesis is an optional deeper pathway from the Verse Box introduction.
14.route: Luke’s personal HBOT purchase and Genesis journey
14.mayoralCouncilLever: Luke’s voluntary participation could provide a personal example for conversations about human agency, learning and personal intelligence. Any council programme or partnership would have its own decision route.
14.outside: Luke would decide his participation, equipment purchase, private records and chosen disclosures. Suppliers, providers and venue owners would retain their own responsibilities.
14.partners: Equipment and software providers, venue and operating partners chosen by Luke, and people he invites into his learning.
14.conflictBoundary: Luke’s personally purchased HBOT equipment and Genesis intellectual property would be relevant interests if council funded, hosted, purchased or arranged access to them.

15.purpose: Co-operative access to health and wellbeing tools could reduce duplicated equipment costs through pooled access.
15.redlandsAdaptation: Community participants and providers could develop membership, ownership, booking, affordability and operating arrangements for shared wellbeing tools. Responsible providers would retain arrangements for clinical services, alongside each person’s care choices.
15.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring community members, providers and co-operative advisers together around shared access. Council could consider relevant public-benefit support through its normal processes.
15.conflictBoundary: Luke’s equipment, provider role or membership interest would be identified in any council-funded shared-access arrangement involving him.

16.purpose: People and carers could spend less effort coordinating support and remain connected to local services as circumstances change.
16.redlandsAdaptation: People, carers and existing providers could co-design everyday assistance and continuity arrangements. Chosen personal information, communication preferences, reminders, local services and meaningful activities could help support follow the person’s changing circumstances.
16.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring community, disability, aged-care and carer organisations together, connecting council’s relevant roles in access, information, venues and community support.
16.conflictBoundary: Luke’s support software, intellectual property or provider role would be a relevant interest if council commissioned or funded everyday support services using it.

17.purpose: Young people could have more opportunities to learn, make, contribute and build trusted relationships across generations.
17.redlandsAdaptation: Supervised learning and creative activities could use age-appropriate AI tools and connect participants with existing youth services. They would follow lawful guardian or care-authority processes, consent or assent appropriate to age and capacity, and the relevant institutional approvals.
17.mayoralCouncilLever: Council could support spaces, opportunities, partnerships and community programmes for young people.
17.outside: Education, children in care, clinical services, police and youth justice remain with the responsible authorities. Their lawful consent and safeguarding arrangements would apply.
17.conflictBoundary: Luke’s youth-learning materials, software or delivery role would be a relevant interest if council funded or commissioned a programme involving them.
